card.name: Reflexive pronoun after take/with/in
card.fires_on: A pronoun or possessive (its, himself, them, you, their, it) that refers back to the subject, right after a preposition like with, in, as, around or upon. Often follows verbs like take or have.

modes.label: Take X with you
modes.description: A pronoun after 'with' that refers back to the subject, in phrases about bringing things along.
modes.example: to take your favorite portable software with<< you>>. Portable application suites like PortableApps.com

modes.label: Take it upon himself / as its focus
modes.description: A reflexive or possessive pronoun in an idiom where it refers back to the subject.
modes.example: Elgar took it upon<< himself>> to be the “looked-for genius

modes.label: Thing containing something
modes.description: A pronoun after 'in' or 'around' that refers back to the thing just described.
modes.example: They have no metal in<< them>>, and can be made translucent or opaque

card.plain: It marks a pronoun like 'them' or 'you' that points back to the subject, as in 'take it with you'.
